title: Safety of an encoded configuration
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $x,v$ be Boolean words, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $v$. Suppose $i\le |v|$, and every work-tape head of $c$ lies between $-S$ and $S$. Form a configuration for the compiled program on input $x$ by retaining $c$'s state, output, original work tapes, and work-head positions, adjoining one extra tape containing the binary expansion of $i$ with its head at $0$, placing the input head at position $1$, and adjoining the phase $\mathrm{ph}$ to the state. Then every work-tape head lies between its prescribed lower and upper bounds (the original tapes between $-S$ and $S$, and the extra tape between $-1$ and the length of the binary expansion of $|v|+1$); moreover, whenever the state is a call state, the input head is at position $1$, the extra-tape head is at $0$, and that tape contains the binary expansion of some integer at most $|v|$.
hypotheses_covered: Every work-tape head of $c$ lies in $[-S,S]$
